thesis: AI can change reproductive costs and cultural transmission in opposite directions, while epistemic pluralism needs rigorous testing.
role: Connect administrative costs, alignment and family institutions.

ideas.statement: Institutions can recruit competence while making its intergenerational renewal difficult.
AI tutors and epistemic mediation may reshape parent-child transmission and community retention.
AI may reduce parenting burdens or substitute for human relationships; both could coexist.
Open hypothesis exploration requires severe testing and correctable disagreement.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A family assistant could handle appointments and logistics; companionship could reduce incentives for relationships.
Sink habitat analogy describes continuing recruitment without internal renewal.
The speculative interface-design claim concerns altered costs of traits, not direct genome engineering.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: The alignment-demography bifurcation is explicitly speculation, not prediction.
Alignment addresses real control/safety problems; epistemic filters have errors in both directions.
False beliefs are not automatically useful diversity.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
